name: fennick
author: school-home
description:
fennick (direction: school and home life) - A BOOKCASE. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

CLUE = "LAYOUT/TALLY". LAYOUT is one row of shelf slots: an uppercase letter = a book standing in that slot, "." = an empty slot. Both ends are always books (the outermost runs have length >= 2), so "is the outside of the shelf a wall or a hole?" never has to be guessed. TALLY is four letter+digit pairs, e.g. "U1E2R2W1". Width 55-62 slots; clue 64-70 chars.

ANSWER = the finished picture: max(h) rows of W characters and then one row of "=" (the shelf). Book j is drawn as a solid bottom-aligned bar of h_j copies of its letter with "." above it. Consequently the bottom text row IS the LAYOUT and the player's only freedom is the heights.

RULE. A book LEANS iff (1) exactly one of its two neighbouring slots is empty - a book with books on both sides is held up, a book with holes on both sides has nothing pushing it over - AND (2) the slot two along in that direction holds a book (the hole is one slot wide; across a two-slot hole there is nothing within reach) AND (3) that book is STRICTLY taller than it (you can only lean on something taller; equal heights and both stay up). score = 1 iff the picture is well formed, its bottom row equals LAYOUT, and for each of the four named letters the number of leaning books of that letter equals its digit. Letters not named in the tally are unconstrained decoys.

Emergent mechanic (and the reason construction is easy once the rule is known): the two books flanking a one-slot hole point at each other, so exactly one of them leans - the shorter - or neither, if you give them the same height. Ties are the only way to zero a pair.

INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH. One demo shows the picture and that its bottom row is the clue's layout, so "the answer is this shelf drawn with heights I choose" is visible immediately; all the remaining difficulty is "which books does the tally count?". generate() plants in every instance at least 4 isolated books (holes on both sides) and 4 books beside a two-slot hole, and deals those decoy slots to the four named letters, so each of the three natural near-misses changes a named tally in most instances. Measured against a 75-law catalogue (which books are counted x what they are compared with x comparison): median 1 demo, max 5, 0 failures in 100 random demo orders. So the class is fair to a player who generates the right catalogue; the whole difficulty is whether "hole on exactly one side + the book two along + strictly taller" ever gets proposed.

DEGENERATE WITNESSES CLOSED (800 fresh clues, shipped scorer). empty / whitespace / junk / "1"*100 / the clue itself / shuffled solution: 0 %. Layout row alone i.e. every book height 1: 0 %; any flat picture (all heights equal): 0 % - generate() never emits a clue whose named tallies are all zero (it requires >= 3 non-zero and a total >= 5). A minimal witness is impossible: the bottom row must equal a 55-62 slot layout. Right-size picture on a shuffled layout: 0 %. Blind random heights 1..9: 1.1 %; 1..3: 0.5 %; sawtooth up: 1.0 %; sawtooth down: 0.8 %. Well-formedness attacks (floating book, two letters in one column, book standing in a declared hole, book missing, extra/absent/wrong shelf row, ragged rows, trailing spaces, mirrored picture): all 0 %, checked by hand. Near-miss rules, where a player holding rule R constructs an answer satisfying R: ">= instead of >" 31 % (falsified by 83 % of demos), "nearest book beyond the hole however wide" 18 % (90 %), "holes on both sides count too" 13 % (92 %), "shorter than a book two away, ignoring holes" 6 %, "shorter than the right neighbour" 0.9 %, "next to exactly one hole, heights irrelevant" 0 % (that rule cannot even hit the tally). KNOWN LOOSENESS, declared: the tally constrains only ~18 of ~40 books, so 86 % of single-book height edits of a correct answer still score 1. That is not a witness (you still need the rule to build one) but the accepted set is large.

ENGINEERING (3000 fresh seeds). generate max 0.89 ms, solve max 17.6 ms, score max 0.57 ms and 0.018 ms on junk; scorer 483/512 chars; clue 64-70 chars, solution 335-609 chars; 3000/3000 clues distinct, deterministic, solve() scores 1 on all of them; 0 disagreements against an independent re-implementation of the rule over 9250 (clue, answer) pairs including malformed ones.
